business_scope.primary_industry_name: Personal Wealth Analytics and Investment Tracking Cloud

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (Napoleonic heritage, reinforced by modern commercial code and directly applicable EU regulations; no US-style common law doctrine of precedent binds the courts)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg-United States Tax Convention (DTA) as amended by 2009 Protocol
Luxembourg-China Double Taxation Agreement on Income and Capital (with related protocols)
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (freedom of establishment, free movement of capital)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (negotiated; pending EU ratification)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (incl. implementing AML Directive (EU) 2015/849, (EU) 2018/843 and (EU) 2018/1673); CSSF Regulation 12-02 on AML/CFT; Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (SCSp provisions); Criminal Code Articles 506-1 onwards on money laundering.
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_narrative: Post ECJ rulings C-37/20 and C-601/20, the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners is not publicly accessible. Access is limited to competent authorities (RCS, AED, CSSF, tax authorities) and AML/CFT obliged entities, with access for other persons granted only upon proof of a legitimate interest in AML/CFT enforcement; SCSp internal UBO data is also disclosed to the RBE and to the issuing bank.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Partnership Agreement (Contrat de Société) of the SCSp
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg notary (authentic deed) or the partners by private deed where opted; notarized form preferred for bank and AML acceptance

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation / Extract of the RCS
Declaration of Beneficial Owners (Déclaration des Bénéficiaires Effectifs)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each UBO and the general partner, filed electronically at the LBR RBE; signatures notarized or certified where required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport or National ID of each UBO, general partner, manager and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport/ID authority of each individual
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (certified true copy) plus sworn translation into French, German or English

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Extract of every corporate UBO and parent entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign company registry (e.g., China SAMR, Hong Kong CR, Delaware SOS)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization for non-Hague Contracting States; sworn translation into an EU official language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Domiciliation Agreement / Lease for the Luxembourg registered office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (professional of the financial sector) or property lessor
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private contract; notarized copy accepted by RCS where required

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-incorporation screening of all UBOs, partners, directors, and authorized signatories against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (incl. UN Security Council resolutions), EU autonomous sanctions, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT Sanctions List, and CSSF/AED national lists; PEP determination per Law of 12 November 2004 requiring enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth documentation, and independent second-level approval for PEP relationships; ongoing monitoring of payment rails (Stripe, Apple IAP) for sanctions and adverse media once operational.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - lbr.lu, including the eJustice RCS online filing portal for name clearance, reservation and registration
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: RCS administration is conducted in French; the proposed corporate name must be available in Latin script and may additionally include a localized or international tradename rendered in Latin characters. Names in non-Latin scripts (e.g., Chinese characters) must be transliterated into Latin script for official registration; a secondary tradename in non-Latin script may coexist only if the primary RCS name is Latin. The legal form must be designated unequivocally as 'Société en Commandite Spéciale' or 'SCSp'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: any token implying state guarantee, public authority, or regulated financial-sector activity without prior ministerial or CSSF approval
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon LBR refusal, counsel files a written administrative reconsideration with the LBR within 15 days of the refusal notice; if the refusal is maintained, a judicial appeal lies to the Tribunal d'Arrondissement de Luxembourg (commercial chamber) under the Code de commerce within one month of notification, with the Luxembourg Public Prosecutor's Office heard on name availability; in parallel, the applicant may submit a revised materially distinct name. Reconsideration carries no additional statutory fee; judicial appeal and counsel drafting fees are market-based.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.statutory_mandate_narrative: The Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies (as amended) requires every SCSp to maintain a registered office in Luxembourg and a real or effective administration centre (siège réel); a letterbox arrangement without local substance may be re-characterized for tax residence, AML, or substance enforcement purposes.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally_Acceptable_With_Licensed_Domiciliation_Agent: for this low-risk fintech SCSp, a pure virtual address without local substance is not accepted by the RCS or the issuing bank; a licensed Luxembourg domiciliation agent (PFS) may supply a registered office, provided substantive local administration exists (Luxembourg-resident general partner or designated manager, local books, records, and meeting facilities) and the register of UBOs is maintained in Luxembourg.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low_Approx_10_Percent_Unannounced_Inspection_Risk_In_First_Operating_Year: RCS review at incorporation is documentary; AED and CSSF AML inspections are risk-based, and for a low-risk software-as-a-service activity the probability of unannounced physical inspection in the first 12 months is estimated at no more than 10%.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_narrative: If triggered, an unannounced inspection would verify physical presence, staff or management access, bookkeeping, UBO records, and availability of the registered office; non-compliance could result in RCS deregistration, CSSF enforcement against any involved PFS, and criminal sanctions under the Law of 12 November 2004.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization of the SCSp partnership agreement (public deed form, recommended for bank and AML counterparty acceptance)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff scale; approx. EUR 650 for standard SCSp deed excluding registration duties

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS inscription fee for registration of the SCSp in the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory filing fee (approx. EUR 75) per Grand-Ducal Regulation on LBR tariffs

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed in the RESA (Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory publication tariff (approx. EUR 19) per electronic notice

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs) filing of ultimate beneficial owners
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: No statutory fee for electronic UBO declaration filing

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Licensed Luxembourg domiciliation and registered office service, year 1 (includes postal handling, UBO archive and AML compliance support)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: approx. EUR 1,350 per annum for fintech entities at low-risk tier

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Market benchmark: approx. EUR 165 per entity per quarter for low-volume screening

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Ministry of Foreign Affairs or consulate of the document's country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory per-document tariffs: approx. USD 30 to USD 50 per apostille or consular certificate

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Sworn translation of non-Latin (e.g., Chinese) corporate and ID documents into French, German, or English
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Court-approved sworn translator in Luxembourg or country of origin
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark: approx. EUR 40 to EUR 60 per page depending on complexity

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 concerning Commercial Companies, as amended (Loi du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), in particular the provisions on partnerships limited by shares and the spéciale limited partnership (SCSp) introduced by subsequent amendment of the law of 12 July 2013.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) acting as registrar for the Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société) together with the RCSL registration declaration (déclaration pour l'inscription au registre de commerce et des sociétés)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: None. An SCSp has no statutory minimum paid-up capital and no court escrow or blocked account requirement. Partner contributions are freely contractually determined and may be made in cash, in kind, or as services, without notarial attestation of payment.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the initial partners have subscribed to the partnership interests set forth in the attached subscription schedule, with the agreed initial contributions to be held by the partnership in accordance with the SCSp partnership agreement. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office of the partnership is fixed at the address designated in the partnership agreement in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that the general partner and the first manager are duly appointed, with authority to open bank accounts, sign regulatory filings, and engage professional advisers. RESOLVED FURTHER, that all taxes, fees and publication charges incident to formation are authorized, and the manager is directed to file the partnership agreement with the Luxembourg Business Registers and complete the registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Prepare and execute the SCSp partnership agreement and obtain name clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – online name availability search (LBR portal)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a corporate name availability search on the Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) portal. Prepare and execute the SCSp partnership agreement (contrat de société), listing all general and limited partners, initial contributions, business purpose, duration, management rules and registered office. The agreement may be a private deed; notarization is optional unless real estate rights are contributed.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of each partner
Certificate of good standing for corporate general partner (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused or flagged as identical or confusing, file a new LBR name reserve request with a proposed alternative and adjust the partnership agreement accordingly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File for registration with the RCSL and obtain the legal existence number
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCSL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed partnership agreement together with the required annexes through the LBR e-filing platform or at the RCSL Guichet Unique. The filing must include the nomination of the general partner and the manager (associé-gérant), the registered office address, and specimen signatures. Payment of the filing and publication fee is made online.
required_dossiers: Nomination and acceptance of the general partner and manager
Consent of the registered office provider
Proof of payment of RCSL filing fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCSL issues a query (observation), respond within 15 days by amending the filing, uploading corrected annexes, or clarifying the missing information; otherwise the file is closed and must be resubmitted.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete mandatory publication in the RESA electronic gazette
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – RESA (Recueil Electronique des Sociétés et Associations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCSL registration, the registry automatically transmits the registration data to RESA for legal publication. Review the published notice and the annexed partnership agreement to verify consistency with the signed facts. The publication is a condition precedent for reliance on the partnership's filings against third parties.
required_dossiers: Copy of the partnership agreement for publication
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains inaccuracies, apply to the RCSL for a rectification filing with the corrected instrument and pay any additional publication fee, if the correction is non-substantive.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain the national identification number and VAT registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) and Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The RCSL registration automatically generates the national business number (matricule). Confirm assignment of the matricule and, if taxable, complete VAT registration via the LBR or the AEDT. For an SCSp that is considered a taxable person, register for VAT if the software analytics services will be taxable in Luxembourg; otherwise complete the simplified service registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the VAT number is not issued, submit a written request to the AEDT with the RCSL extract and partnership agreement; any discrepancy is cured within 20 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as an employer and satisfy social security reporting (if staff engaged)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: If the SCSp will hire employees, register as an employer with the CCSS and obtain the social security affiliation number. File the initial employer declaration with employee details. This registration is autonomous from the RCSL and is required before any payroll liability is incurred.
required_dossiers: Identity and civil status documents of initial employees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the CCSS declares the file incomplete, provide the requested employee documentation within 10 working days; late registration is cured by retroactive affiliation with potential administrative penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) – Directorate for Industry and Digitalisation
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not required – the registered business activity is a personal wealth analytics and investment-tracking software service, falling outside industrial establishment and manufacturing licensing regimes.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – no physical installation, effluent generation, or production facility; no full EIA or environmental registration is required for a cloud-software administrative office.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable – the activity produces no wastewater streams, VOC emissions, or hazardous waste. The office tenant relies on existing building systems; all cloud servers are hosted by certified third-party data centers subject to EU energy efficiency standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety conformity certification for the registered office under the communal fire-prevention regulations; occupational safety registration with the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM); no structural load inspection is required for standard administrative premises.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct taxes; Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT; Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) for entity registration; single digital government portal: MyGuichet.lu / guichet.lu, with electronic filing via the eCDF module of the tax authority.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Execute the SCSp limited partnership agreement before a Luxembourg notary and file the constitutive dossier with the RCS Luxembourg, which issues an 11-digit national business registration number ('matricule') that serves as the statutory corporate tax reference. Step 2: Submit the VAT registration application (Formulaire 640/641 as applicable) to the AEDT through MyGuichet; the AEDT issues a Luxembourg VAT identification number in the format 'LU' + 8 digits. Registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable turnover for any person carrying out an economic activity in Luxembourg; no minimum capital is required and 100% foreign ownership is permitted. Step 3: Register with the Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS) if the SCSp employs staff. Step 4: Non-resident partners do not require a Luxembourg TIN unless a Luxembourg permanent establishment or Luxembourg-source income exists; the entity matricule remains the sole direct-tax reference for the partnership.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Pass_Through_Eligible: The SCSp is a contractual partnership without separate legal personality and is mandatorily fiscally transparent for Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) and municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal); income is allocated to partners and taxed at their level. The SCSp is not a separate taxpayer for Luxembourg net wealth tax, and no minimum net wealth tax applies at entity level. For VAT, the SCSp is independently a taxable person where it conducts an economic activity. Territorial scope: resident partners are taxed on worldwide income, with the participation exemption (95% exemption for qualifying dividends and capital gains) available; non-resident partners are taxable only on Luxembourg-source income, principally through a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box or general optional entity classification exists under Luxembourg domestic law; partnership transparency is compulsory. Statutory elections available: (i) small-business VAT franchise election under Article 57 VAT Law where annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000; (ii) if the SCSp qualifies as an 'investment entity' under the EU Minimum Tax Directive (2022/2523, implemented by the Luxembourg law of 22 December 2023), an election to be treated as a Tax Transparent Investment Vehicle (TTIV) or Taxable Investment Vehicle (TIV) for GloBE/Pillar 2 purposes; (iii) joint VAT-group election (assujetti unique) under Article 22(1) VAT Law; (iv) One-Stop-Shop (OSS) registration election for EU-wide B2C electronically supplied services; (v) partner-level use of the participation exemption and ATAD-compliant hybrid-mismatch consistency elections for cross-border investors.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Luxembourg Value Added Tax (TVA), governed by the Luxembourg VAT Law of 12 February 1979 as amended, in accordance with EU Directive 2006/112/EC
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No general registration threshold for Luxembourg-established taxable persons: registration is mandatory from the first euro of taxable turnover. A small-business franchise exemption is available where annual taxable turnover does not exceed EUR 35,000 and quarterly turnover does not exceed EUR 8,750, subject to conditions and prior claims; the franchise cannot be used for intra-Community acquisitions or imports. Non-established suppliers of digital services to Luxembourg consumers are required to VAT-register either directly or via the OSS; the SCSp developing the financial-portfolio-tracking App should use the Union OSS scheme to declare B2C electronic supplies in all EU Member States of the consumer.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: B2G electronic invoicing has been mandatory since 1 January 2024 through the Luxembourg central e-invoicing portal in PEPPOL format. A mandatory B2B e-invoicing regime for domestic transactions is scheduled for 1 July 2026 (implementation decrees pending, aligned with the EU ViDA package). Luxembourg does not currently apply a real-time fiscal pre-clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction controls regime; the model is post-audit with electronic archiving. Taxpayers must accept structured electronic invoices (EN 16931-conformant) and retain SAF-T-style electronic files and the EC Sales List (recapitulative statement) for intra-EU supplies.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: (1) Goods: physical exports to a destination outside the EU qualify for the 0% VAT rate under Article 56 VAT Law where dispatch or transport to a third country is evidenced; intra-EU supplies qualify for 0% domestic VAT with a valid customer VAT ID and inclusion in the EC Sales List. (2) Services: B2B supplies of the financial-portfolio-tracking software are outside Luxembourg VAT where the customer is established outside Luxembourg (EU customer: reverse charge; non-EU customer: no Luxembourg VAT). (3) B2C electronically supplied services are taxed where the consumer is established: 17% Luxembourg VAT applies only to Luxembourg-resident consumers; supplies to other EU consumers are reported through OSS at the consumer-state rate; supplies to non-EU consumers fall outside the scope of EU VAT. (4) Exemption note: only if the App genuinely performs discretionary management of special investment funds (UCITS/AIF) does the Article 44(1)(m) VAT exemption apply; standard analytics and portfolio-tracking functionality constitutes a taxable digital service at the standard rate and is not eligible for zero-rating.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (Single Administrative Document - SAD/DAU) with Movement Reference Number
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR consignment note evidencing physical exit from the EU
Commercial invoices and bank transfer records (SWIFT/SEPA) evidencing payment of subscription or licence fees
Proof of customer establishment (VAT registration certificate, tax residence certificate, or business registry extract)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank account statements showing receipt of the foreign consideration in the SCSp's bank account
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Luxembourg law does not impose a formal statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark is applied as the operational documentary-retention standard for export substantiation. If the exporter cannot produce the complete evidentiary bundle, the AEDT may claw back the zero rating: VAT becomes payable at the standard rate (17%) plus late-payment interest of 0.8% per month and late-filing surcharges (up to 10%). Fraudulent export zero-rating, forged transport documents, or sham disposal of goods constitute criminal VAT fraud under Article 71 of the VAT Law, attracting fines up to EUR 250,000, imprisonment of up to 5 years, administrative penalties of up to 200% of the evaded VAT, and a reassessment period extended from 5 to 10 years. Incorrect OSS filings trigger additional penalties in the Member State of consumption.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) together with the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking licensing and AML/CTF oversight of financial market participants.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg is a full member of the European Union and the Eurozone; the euro is freely convertible on both current and capital accounts. No exchange controls, no approval requirements for inward or outward remittances, profit repatriation, dividend distribution, or liquidation proceeds. Capital and money market operations are fully liberalized under EU Treaty provisions and the Capital Movement Directive. The only administrative obligation is statistical reporting to the BCL for balance-of-payments (BoP) and international investment position (IIP) purposes when cross-border flows exceed de minimis thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No statutory requirement to surrender export proceeds or maintain mandatory conversion ratios. Luxembourg does not impose any repatriation, holding, or conversion obligations on export receipts; proceeds may be retained in any currency. Reporting to BCL is limited to BoP statistical filings for transactions exceeding EUR 12,500 as part of the monthly reporting framework for enterprises engaged in external trade.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium feasibility only for ancillary payment facilitation. A locally authorized Electronic Money Institution (EMI) under CSSF, or an EU passported EMI from another EEA state, can legally open a corporate account and provide IBANs, payment initiation, and virtual accounts. However, for the SCSp as an unregulated private investment vehicle, any EMI solution is not a substitute for a Tier-1 bank account due to regulatory capital constraints, higher compliance requirements, and the absence of commercial lending or treasury management infrastructure. Restricted-use sub-accounts may be acceptable for low-risk software subscriptions, but the primary treasury account must be held with a fully licensed credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: A physical appearance of the general partner (GP) or managers is not strictly mandatory when the bank's remote digital onboarding system (audio-video identification) is used, provided the applicant is an EEA national or equivalent. For non-EEA beneficial owners or where the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) is a private trust or another partnership, a bank may require an in-person interview at the branch or at a Luxembourg notary's office. In all cases, identification of the SCSp itself requires a certified extract from the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), the partnership agreement (limited partnership agreement or articles), and a declaration of the authorized signatories, with original power-of-attorney if so stipulated. Remote opening is permitted for low-risk structures with a fully remote KYC workflow, but the bank retains the right to require a physical or legalized-document lift at any stage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex multi-layer ownership: SCSp with anonymous or discretionary private trust as ultimate beneficiary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a full organizational chart, trust deed or written declaration of legal ownership, and confirmation that the trust is not established under an opaque secrecy jurisdiction. Include a signed confirmation of source of funds and material wealth; a legal opinion from a Luxembourg or EU counsel confirming the economic substance and non-regulated status; and a brief business narrative demonstrating no connection with tax evasion, PEP, or higher-risk activities.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of non-EEA digital payment service providers (e.g., US-licensed EMIs, Singapore/Malta payment services) as the sole historical financial intermediary
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Supply transactional history from the past 12 months, proof of licensing or authorization of the payment provider in its home jurisdiction, a clear explanation of the reason for using that provider, and a representation letter confirming that channel is not used for revenue settlement. Provide the new bank with a list of expected transaction categories and counterparties using SWIFT or SEPA statement evidence.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SCSp capital contributions sourced from crypto-assets or virtual currency conversions
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide blockchain analytics report from a recognized firm (Chainalysis, Elliptic) showing the source of cryptocurrency proceeds, signed documentation of the purchase/sale transactions, evidence of high-quality AML/CTF controls in the crypto exchange (EU regulated exchanges only), and a legal confirmation that the SCSp has no exposure to digital assets in its investment policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume anticipated cross-border payments to jurisdictions with elevated money-laundering risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare a counterparty due-diligence file for every material trade partner (legal entity checklist, UBO identification, proof of business activity, no negative sanctions screening), segment counterparties by jurisdiction, and provide a written covenant that all payments will be made only to the exact beneficiary listed in the software license agreements and invoices. Include a sanctions self-screening policy and periodic transaction monitoring plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Director or authorized signatory is a politically exposed person (PEP) or family member of a PEP
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a detailed declaration of PEP status, source of wealth and source of funds for all capital contributions to the SCSp, an independent credit report if available, tax/wealth disclosures, and consent to enhanced ongoing monitoring. The dossier must also include a notarized or apostilled letter confirming no conflict of interest is connected to Luxembourg public procurement or state assets.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All capital contributions and shareholder loans to the SCSp must be paid from a verified corporate or personal bank account in the name of the capital provider to the SCSp's designated RMB receipt account (or a EUR account at a Tier-1 bank). Wire transfers must carry an accurate purpose code and a clear reference to the capital contribution clause of the partnership agreement. Under Luxembourg BCL statistical reporting, any inbound transfer exceeding EUR 12,500 must be reported in the monthly BoP declaration with the proper classification code for direct investment (e.g., participation in capital) or loans. No forex conversion is required; the euro is the reporting currency and the SCSp may maintain multi-currency accounts. Inbound transfers from non-EEA jurisdictions must include a full remitter name, address, and UBO/beneficial ownership breakdown to satisfy the CSSF's AML/CFT rulebook (Regulation 12-02), and the bank will verify the underlying documentation (capital contribution statement, notarized resolution where requested) before credit.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade settlements should be made via SWIFT MT103 or MT202 for cryptocurrency-independent software SaaS payments; for invoice settlements above an agreed bank threshold, an MT103 with field 70 specifying the service description and invoice number is standard. Commercial letters of credit (L/C) are generally not required for low-risk digital services but may be used when the SCSp expands into physical infrastructure or high-value subscription licensing, in which case a confirmed irrevocable L/C issued by a Luxembourg or EU bank is recommended. For SEPA-based recurring payments within the EEA, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is the default rail with a maximum execution time of 1 business day. All outbound disbursements must be backed by the underlying contractual agreements kept in the SCSp's treasury record; no cash or bearer-instrument disbursements are permitted. The bank will apply the same sanctions and embargo checks to every payment with a confirmation receipt generated via SWIFT FIN services or the commercial bank's API.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX Forwards – Over-the-counter (OTC) euro vs. USD/GBP/CHF/SGD fixed-date forwards, provided the SCSp has genuine commercial exposure under its software subscription and payment receipts; no leveraged speculative trades.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) – Permissible only for illiquid or restricted currencies (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) where an onshore forward is not obtainable; must be documented as hedging actual forecasted receivables or payables with a 12-month tenor cap.

FX Swaps – Cross-currency swaps (fixed-floating, EUR-USD/EUR-GBP) allowed when the SCSp has long-term multi-currency investments, subject to EMIR central clearing and trade repository reporting if the counterparty is a major bank or the notional exceeds the €8 billion threshold; otherwise uncleared swaps are permitted with bilateral margining.
Exchange-Traded Currency Futures – Permitted for listed contracts on EU or EEA exchanges (e.g., Euronext) with daily margin posting, subject to the SCSp's treasury governance manual.

FX Options (plain-vanilla call/put) – Allowed only for hedging actual economic flows and not for speculative income; written approval from the appointed bank relationship manager and execution through an established clearing member is required.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Statutory Accounts Deposit (comptes annuels) — publication of annual financial statements; exempt where the general partner is subject to the EU Directive 2013/34/EU transparency regime
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Trade and Companies Register (RCS) via the eJustice portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months after the balance-sheet date; for a calendar-year SCSp, due by 31 July of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Judicial fines of EUR 1,250–10,000 per officer; court injunction to publish accounts under a daily penalty (astreinte); persistent failure triggers compulsory judicial dissolution and RCS strike-off.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Beneficial Ownership Register (RBE) Declaration and Annual Substantial-Change Confirmation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Register of Beneficial Owners (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs, RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Event-driven: within one month of any change in the ownership chain; standing duty to keep data current, checked annually during the register audit cycle
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines of EUR 1,250–250,000 per entity or officer for false, incomplete, or late declarations; RESA publication of the conviction; potential restriction of profit distributions.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Pass-Through Partnership Income Tax Information Return (fiscally transparent SCSp)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 31 December of the year following the close of the tax year; extension until 31 March of the next year available on request to the ACD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: 10% late-filing surcharge computed on the tax due; default interest of 0.6% per month; ex officio assessment by the ACD; administrative fines of EUR 1,200–25,000 imposed on the general partner.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Register Audit, Partnership Meeting Minutes, and Statutory Books Updating (internal secretarial deliverable)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: No external filing; records kept at the registered office and produced on demand to RCS, ACD, and notaries
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Prior to the annual partnership meeting provided for in the partnership agreement; in no case later than 12 months after the balance-sheet date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Civil liability of the general partner for deficient or incomplete statutory books; criminal penalties only where falsification or fraudulent concealment is established.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: The SCSp lacks legal personality and benefits from the statutory exemption from the EU audit and publication regime where the general partner is itself subject to publication under Directive 2013/34/EU. An independent statutory audit becomes mandatory where (i) the partnership agreement requires it, (ii) the vehicle is used as a regulated fund under CSSF/RAIF/SIF rules, or (iii) the SCSp exceeds, for two consecutive years, at least two of three thresholds: balance sheet total above EUR 4,400,000, net turnover above EUR 8,800,000, and average headcount above 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP as codified by the law of 19 December 2008 on annual accounts (transposing Directive 2013/34/EU); IFRS may be adopted voluntarily; CSSF-regulated fund arrangements require either Lux GAAP or IFRS in accordance with CSSF circulars.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Under the Luxembourg RBE law of 13 January 2019, the SCSp must maintain a continuous and accurate beneficial-ownership file. The general partner must reconcile the Register of Limited Partners against the RBE file at each annual cycle, because any transfer of partnership interests takes effect against third parties only upon registration. Qualifying changes are reportable to the RBE within one month; a formal yearly re-filing is not separately prescribed, but the annual reconciliation constitutes the de facto confirmation event, including for non-resident partners in the ownership chain.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Limited Partners (associés commanditaires) including all transfers of partnership interests
Register of General Partners and Management (associés commandités)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700–2,500 per year (registered office facilities and corporate secretarial services in Luxembourg City)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000–8,000 for a small SCSp; USD 12,000–25,000 where a CSSF-type fund audit is required

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg IP regime provides an 80% exemption of qualifying intellectual property income, producing an effective tax rate of approximately 5.42% on eligible IP-derived revenue. The participation exemption offers 100% exclusion on qualified dividend income and capital gains. As a Société en Commandite Spéciale (SCSp) is fiscally transparent, entity-level CIT is generally not triggered; profits are allocated to partners and taxed according to their residence and treaty status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 820 (Corporate Income Tax Return, impôt sur les sociétés) filed via the Luxembourg direct tax portal MyTax/eTVA (Administration des contributions directes). For a fiscally transparent SCSp, no separate entity-level Form 820 is required unless the entity has elected or is classified as taxable for Luxembourg tax purposes.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Filing is due by 31 May of the calendar year following the fiscal year-end; extensions to 31 December may be granted upon reasoned request. Corporate partners must file their shareholder-level declarations within the same deadlines.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable profit of the taxpayer after commercial-law adjustments, disallowable expenses, and tax-exempt participation income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident partners of an SCSp are not subject to Luxembourg corporate tax on their allocable share unless the SCSp operates through a Luxembourg permanent establishment. If no PE exists, no Luxembourg form is required at partner level.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Participation exemption deduction: 100% of qualifying dividend income and capital gains from a 10% or EUR 1,200,000-participation held for at least 12 months.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a transparent SCSp, the participation exemption is assessed at the corporate partner level, subject to proof of holding period and voting rights; treaty-protected non-resident partners must retain documentation of the underlying ownership chain.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net wealth tax computation and minimum annual contribution for resident companies subject to the impôt sur la fortune.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: An SCSp engaged in financial portfolio tracking and asset holding is normally exempt from Luxembourg net wealth tax; non-resident partners have no net wealth filing obligation in Luxembourg.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers administrative penalties ranging from EUR 250 to EUR 2,500 per return, plus default interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid tax up to 24% maximum. Material false declarations may attract a penalty up to 20% of the tax evaded and criminal sanctions for fraud.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: A reduced rate or zero rate under a Luxembourg income tax treaty is implemented by filing Form 22 (request for withholding tax relief at source) with the Luxembourg tax administration, attaching a valid Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the treaty partner and evidence of beneficial ownership. For retroactive claims, Form 22bis is used to request a refund of excess withholding tax. The parent-subsidiary directive applies where a qualifying EU parent holds at least 10% of the SCSp's rights and the holding period meets at least 12 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law does not impose withholding tax on interest or royalty payments to non-residents absent a Luxembourg permanent establishment. The EU Interest and Royalties Directive secures a 0% rate for associated enterprises qualifying with a 25% direct holding for at least two years. Treaty rates are generally 0% for interest and royalties under Luxembourg DTA practice.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File required when controlled transactions with related parties exceed EUR 100,000 per counterparty per fiscal year; Master File required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue above EUR 50,000,000; Country-by-Country Report threshold is EUR 750,000,000 group turnover.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg enforces the ATAD general anti-abuse rule and the OECD economic-substance standard. An SCSp claiming Luxembourg tax residence or treaty benefits must demonstrate real operational substance in Luxembourg: qualified decision-making employees, registered physical office, actual board meetings, own risk management, and proportionate expenditure. Passive shell or cash-box SCSp structures used without genuine substance are recharacterized and denied residence certificates.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally omitting subscription revenue from the financial portfolio-tracking SaaS platform, inflating deductible IT expenses, and routing profits through the SCSp without any actual service or production activity, causing a phantom tax loss.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment for up to 10 years, default interest of 0.6% per month, fiscal penalty up to 25% of the underpaid tax, and criminal sanctions including imprisonment up to five years and fines up to EUR 1,000,000 under Luxembourg tax fraud provisions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners and directors who sign or approve knowingly false tax declarations are jointly and severally liable for the evaded tax. Courts may order freezing of personal assets, travel bans, director disqualification, and imprisonment in serious cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Artificial Transfer Pricing and Base Erosion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying more than 95% of platform revenue as management, IP licensing, or intra-group service fees to an offshore related company while leaving no profit or substance in Luxembourg, without benchmarking, intercompany agreements, or transfer pricing documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax administration applies the arm's length principle, recharacterizes the transactions, adjusts Luxembourg taxable income, disallows abusive deductions, imposes penalties up to EUR 100,000 plus monthly interest, and may deny treaty relief where arrangement lacks commercial rationality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors approving non-arm's length payments are personally liable for resulting corporate tax, and a Luxembourg court may pierce the corporate veil if the SCSp is used as a pure conduit for abusive profit stripping, including personal attachment orders.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the SCSp without real employees, rented office, independent management, operational bank account in Luxembourg, or actual risk-bearing capacity, while claiming Luxembourg tax residence, DTA access, and EU benefits solely from the registration address.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Refusal or retroactive withdrawal of Luxembourg tax residence certificate, denial of treaty withholding relief, full re-taxation in Luxembourg under GAAR, administrative fines up to EUR 100,000, and mandatory strike-off if the RBE or trade register data are false.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: General partners and formal directors may be held civilly liable for restitution of unpaid taxes; criminal investigation may lead to asset freeze, travel prohibition, individual fines up to EUR 250,000, or imprisonment for fraudulent use of corporate form.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to file the beneficial ownership declaration with the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE) within 30 days of creation or any ownership change, and failure to implement KYC/AML controls for embedded payment rails, including anonymous Stripe and Apple IAP transactions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fines for RBE non-compliance up to EUR 250,000 and daily penalty of EUR 250 per day; AML Law 2019 sanctions up to EUR 1,000,000 and imprisonment up to four years; regulatory prohibition of future payments and business restriction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Managing partners, compliance officers, and beneficial owners incur personal criminal liability, civil damages, disqualification from managerial roles, travel bans, seizure of personal and corporate assets, and imprisonment where the platform is used for money laundering.
